title: How Far Out Should You Book Hardwood Installation in Everett? Lead Times Explained
meta: Book Everett hardwood installation 3 to 6 weeks ahead in spring and summer, 1 to 3 in winter. Wills Flooring on material lead times, acclimation and $3.25.

blocks.lead: Book hardwood installation in Everett three to six weeks before you want the crew in the house during spring and summer, and one to three weeks ahead from November through February.
blocks.detail: The crew's calendar is rarely the bottleneck. Material is. In-stock engineered plank from our distributor arrives in about a week, special-order wide plank can take six to eight, and unfinished solid needs a week in your house before anyone nails it down.

blocks.html: Everett homeowners tend to ask this question with a date attached: the Boeing shutdown week, a kid leaving for college, a Silver Lake listing that needs to hit the market by May. The honest answer is that the day we can show up depends less on our schedule than on what you pick and what we find under the old floor. This post lays out every piece of the timeline, from the first visit to the day the furniture goes back, so you can count backward from your deadline instead of hoping.

blocks.text: The five lead times stacked inside one project

items.text: We bring samples to the house, measure, check the subfloor and moisture, and hand you a firm written quote. From Riverside or Eastmont this is usually booked within two or three days of your call.
items.note: The Lynnwood showroom is about 15 minutes away, so same-week visits are normal.

items.text: In-stock engineered from Metropolitan Hardwood ships in about a week. Special colors, wide plank and long lengths run four to eight weeks. Unfinished solid oak is usually stocked.
items.note: This is the number that decides your date.

items.text: Solid and unfinished hardwood sits in the rooms it will be installed in until its moisture matches the subfloor. Engineered needs less, usually two to three days. Everett's damp winters and dry furnace air both matter here.

Pulling carpet or old vinyl, fixing squeaks, sistering a soft joist in a 1920s Bayside house or flattening a 1990s slab in Silver Lake. Quoted at the estimate, and it can add a day you did not plan for.
A crew installs roughly 300 to 500 sq ft of nail-down per day. A 1,200 sq ft Eastmont main floor is three days; stairs add about a day per flight.
items.note: Unfinished floors add three to five days of sanding, finishing and cure after this.

blocks.text: What quietly pushes your date out

items.title: The spring rush
items.text: From mid-April to Labor Day every Everett contractor is busy. Refinish and install calendars fill three to six weeks out, and the same is true of the distributors' trucks. If your deadline is June, order in April.

items.title: Surprises under the carpet
items.text: 1990s builder homes in Silver Lake often have particleboard underlayment that must come out before nail-down. Older homes in Riverside hide soft spots near the kitchen. Each fix is a day.

items.title: A wet subfloor
items.text: If the plywood meters above 12 percent or the slab fails a moisture test, installation waits until it dries or gets a barrier. Winter installs in a house that has been empty and unheated are the usual culprit.

items.title: Condo and HOA notice
items.text: Port Gardner and downtown Everett buildings often want two weeks' notice, a certificate of insurance and elevator booking. Start that paperwork the day you sign, not the week before.

blocks.text: Book now or wait? An honest comparison

a.title: Lock a date when
items: You have a hard deadline like a listing, a move-in or a family event
You have chosen the plank and it is in stock
The house is occupied and heated so acclimation starts on arrival
You want spring or summer; those weeks go first

b.title: Do not book yet when
items: You have not seen the sample in your own light; a rushed pick is the most expensive mistake
Painting, drywall or a kitchen remodel is still generating dust and moisture
The subfloor needs repair you have not scheduled
You are still deciding between refinishing the old oak and installing new

blocks.title: The most common Everett scheduling mistake:
blocks.text: Booking the install date first and choosing the floor second. The plank you fall for is special order, the date slides six weeks, and the painter you lined up behind us is gone. Pick the floor at the estimate, then set the date around its lead time.
How to shorten your timeline without cutting corners

items.html: Choose from in-stock lines first. Our mobile showroom carries the engineered oaks and hickories that ship in a week. Ask which samples on the ring are stocked before you fall for one that is not.
Take delivery early. Material can sit in your house for two weeks as easily as two days. Acclimation runs while you wait for the crew, not after.
Do the demo yourself if you are able. Pulling carpet and pad on a Saturday can save a day of crew time, though we still remove staples and check the subfloor.
Ask about a winter slot. December through February in Everett usually books one to three weeks out and material moves faster too. Heated, occupied homes install just as well in winter.

Get everything on one written quote. Labor, material, removal, subfloor prep and stairs. A change order mid-job costs more time than money. Our hardwood installation page lists what a Wills quote includes.
Write down your real deadline, then subtract material lead time, acclimation, prep and install days. That is your order-by date.
Book the free estimate now, even if the project is months away. Measured square footage and a subfloor check make every later step faster.
Confirm stock on the exact SKU, including treads and transitions, before you sign.
Plan to keep the house at 60 to 75°F from delivery through install. Vacant Riverside rentals in winter need the heat on early.
Send HOA paperwork the day you sign if you live in a Port Gardner or downtown building.

faq.q: How far in advance should I book hardwood floor installation in Everett?
faq.a: Three to six weeks ahead from April through September, and one to three weeks ahead in winter. Add the material lead time on top if you choose a special-order plank, which can be another four to eight weeks.

faq.q: How long does hardwood flooring take to arrive after ordering?
faq.a: In-stock engineered plank from our distributor arrives in about five to ten days. Special-order widths and colors take four to eight weeks. Unfinished solid oak is usually one to two weeks, then it acclimates in your home before installation.

faq.q: Can I skip acclimation to speed things up?
faq.a: Not for solid or unfinished hardwood. Wood that goes down before it matches the house's moisture gaps or cups within a season, and no installer will warranty it. Engineered plank needs less time, typically two or three days, but still needs it.

faq.q: Is it faster to install hardwood in winter in Everett?
faq.a: Usually. Crews book one to three weeks out and distributors have stock. The house must be heated and dry, and acclimation can take a few extra days because outdoor air is damp, but the calendar itself is far more open.

faq.q: How long does the installation itself take?
faq.a: Roughly 300 to 500 sq ft per day for nail-down engineered or solid, so a 1,200 sq ft main floor is about three days. Stairs add about a day per flight. Unfinished floors add three to five days for sanding, finishing and cure.

faq.q: What if the material arrives short or damaged?
faq.a: We order 7 to 10 percent extra for cuts and waste, and we inspect boxes on delivery. A short order on a special-order product is the one thing that can add weeks, which is why we confirm quantities from measured square footage, not your listing's number.
